minutes.summary: The two-member Board of Trust Fund Commissioners voted to send an addendum to its formal breach notice, a letter to the Attorney General's Public Charities Division, a demand letter to the school department, and a letter to State Senator John Cronin, all asserting that the town and select board willfully refused to fund or authorize warrant articles meant to fix decades of neglected charitable trust administration. The commission also reviewed its annual report materials for town meeting, noted an open vacancy, and set its next meeting for April 23rd.

what_happened.line: Commission voted 2-0 to tell the Attorney General the town willfully refused to fix decades of trust fund breaches.
It also voted to demand the school department account for scholarships and gifts held under the town's tax ID.
A letter asking State Senator John Cronin for emergency help was approved, citing restricted trust funds and unpaid earnings.
The chair held back posting breach-notice materials online pending confirmation of ADA accessibility requirements.
The board authorized the chair to write its own report on commission activities for the town moderator.

why_it_matters: Town meeting will hear this dispute directly, since the select board already denied the commission's warrant articles to fund trust-fund fixes.
The demand letter over school-held scholarships and gifts could surface obligations the school department has not disclosed under the town's own tax identification number.
Escalating to the Attorney General's Public Charities Division and a state senator raises the possibility of state intervention in how the town administers its charitable trusts.
